item.title: Prepare with a Focus on Reviewing Grades 1-2 Curriculum... It's Okay If Scores Are Low (1~2학년 과정 복습 위주로 대비…성적 낮아도 괜찮아요)
item.description:
The National United Achievement Test (hereafter referred to as the Academic Assessment), the first mock exam for the CSAT for high school seniors taking the 2027 College Scholastic Ability Test, will be held on March 24th. This exam is administered by the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education, not the Korea Institute for Curriculum and Evaluation (KICE), which is the CSAT testing agency. Graduates do not take it, and its scope of questions differs from the actual CSAT, which will be held on November 19th, limiting its use for college admissions decisions. (2027학년도 대학수학능력시험을 치르는 고교 3학년의 첫 수능 모의고사인 전국연합학력평가(이하 학평)가 3월24일에 치러진다. 이번 시험은 수능 출제기관인 한국교육과정평가원이 아닌 서울교육청이 주관하고, 졸업생이 응시하지 않으며, 11월19일 치러지는 실제 수능과 출제범위 등이 달라 입시에 활용하기에는 한계가 있다.)

However, the March Academic Assessment is a prime opportunity to objectively evaluate one's skills so far and identify your current position, weak areas, and specific units. Since it's the first mock exam after becoming a senior, the pressure might be considerable, but you should keep in mind that it is a 'practice test' and use it as a chance to gain practical experience. Based on data from Jinhaksa Admissions Strategy Research Institute, Visang Education Admissions Assessment Center, 1318 University Admissions Research Institute, Etoos Education Assessment Research Institute, and Uway Education Assessment Research Institute, we have compiled preparation and utilization strategies for the March Academic Assessment. (하지만 3월 학평은 지금까지 본인의 실력을 객관적으로 평가해 현재 자신의 위치와 취약영역과 단원 등을 파악할 수 있는 절호의 기회다. 고3이 되고나서 치르는 첫 모의고사라는 점에서 부담이 적지 않겠지만, ‘연습시험’이라는 점을 염두에 두고 실전 경험을 쌓는 기회로 삼아야 한다. 진학사 입시전략연구소, 비상교육 입시평가소, 1318대학진학연구소, 이투스 교육평가연구소, 유웨이 교육평가연구소의 자료를 바탕으로 3월 학평 대비 및 활용법을 정리했다.)

Prepare by Focusing on Review and Concept Organization (복습과 개념 정리 위주로 대비)

The March Academic Assessment is a test to gauge how much you have studied so far. Its main purpose is to provide individual scores and grades. Therefore, rather than simply studying hard to do well on the March exam, you should prepare with the mindset of assessing your current skill level. (3월 학평은 지금까지 본인이 얼마나 공부를 해왔는지를 가늠하는 시험이다. 개인별 성적과 등급 등을 제공하는 데 주된 목적이 있다. 이 때문에 단순히 3월 학평을 잘 보기 위해 공부를 하기보다는 현재 내 실력이 어느 정도인지 판단해보자는 마음으로 준비해야 한다.)

The scope of the March Academic Assessment is the entire curriculum for grades 1 and 2 for Korean Language and English, the entire common subjects Mathematics I and Mathematics II for Mathematics, and for elective subjects: Probability and Statistics covers 'I. Number of Cases', Calculus covers 'I. Limits of Sequences', and Geometry covers 'I. Conic Sections'. In other words, since questions come only from what was learned in grades 1 and 2, it is advantageous to review, focusing on your weak areas or vulnerable units from up to the second year before the test. After this period, there won't be many chances for review, so it's better to treat this opportunity as the final period to dedicate yourself to review. (3월 학평은 출제 범위가 국어와 영어 영역의 경우 고등학교 1, 2학년 전 범위, 수학 영역은 공통 과목인 수학Ⅰ, 수학Ⅱ 전 범위이고, 선택 과목인 확률과통계는 ‘Ⅰ. 경우의 수’, 미적분은 ‘Ⅰ. 수열의 극한’, 기하는 ‘Ⅰ. 이차곡선’ 등이다. 즉 1, 2학년 때 배운 내용에서만 출제되는 점을 감안, 시험 전에는 2학년 때까지 본인이 부족한 영역이나 취약 단원 위주로 복습을 하며 준비하는 것이 유리하다. 이 시기를 지나면 복습할 수 있는 기회가 많지 않기 때문에 이번 기회를 마지막 복습에 매진하는 기간으로 삼는 것이 낫다는 것이다.)

Yoo Seong-ryong, head of the 1318 University Admissions Research Institute, said, "If your grades by subject in the Academic Assessments taken up to the second year were within grades 1 or 2, it's fine to do preparatory study using past CSAT questions or EBS CSAT textbooks. However, if you were grade 3 or lower, reviewing the grades 1 and 2 curriculum for each subject is more important than preparatory CSAT study." In this regard, he recommended thoroughly reviewing the textbooks and reference books you have used so far. (유성룡 1318대학진학연구소장은 “2학년 때까지 치른 학력평가의 영역별 등급이 1, 2등급 이내였다면, 그동안 출제된 수능시험 기출 문제나 EBS 수능특강 등을 통해 선행적인 대비를 해도 괜찮다”며 “하지만 3등급 이하였다면 선행적인 수능시험 대비보다는 교과목별로 고교 1, 2학년 과정을 다시 복습하는 것이 무엇보다 중요하다”고 말했다. 이와 관련해 유 소장은 지금껏 봐온 교과서나 참고서 등을 꼭 다시 한번 복습하길 권했다.)

Additionally, Yoo Seong-ryong said, "Study time per subject for students with grades of 3 or lower may vary depending on individual achievement in each subject. However, I suggest that students aiming for mid-to-upper-tier liberal arts programs allocate study time in the order Korean Language > Mathematics > Social Studies > English, and students aiming for science programs in the order Mathematics > Science > Korean Language > English." (또한, 유성룡 소장은 “3등급 이하 학생들의 교과목별 공부 시간은 학생 개개인의 과목별 성취도에 따라 차이가 있을 수 있다”면서도 “하지만 중상위권 인문계 모집단위 지원 학생은 국어 > 수학 > 사회탐구 > 영어 순으로, 자연계 모집단위 지원 학생은 수학 > 과학탐구 > 국어 > 영어 순으로 비중을 두고, 그에 따른 학습 시간을 배정하고 공부했으면 한다”고 제안했다.)

Woo Yeon-cheol, head of Jinhaksa Admissions Strategy Research Institute, advised, "With the March Academic Assessment approaching, some students try to solve a massive number of problems hastily. But the process of organizing and filling gaps in concepts is more important than just solving problems. Using your existing textbooks, you need to check and firmly organize concepts you don't know well or repeatedly get wrong, focusing on incorrect answers." (우연철 진학사 입시전략연구소장은 “3월 학평이 얼마 남지 않은 시점에서 급한 마음에 무작정 많은 문제를 풀려는 학생들이 있다. 하지만 이런 문제 풀이보다는 부족한 개념을 정리해가는 학습 과정이 더 중요하다”며 “기존 교재를 가지고 틀린 문제를 중심으로 자신이 잘 모르는 개념, 반복적으로 틀리는 개념 등을 확인하고 확실히 정리하는 것이 필요하다”고 조언했다.)

Once you've organized concepts to a certain degree, solving past exam questions from the last three years is recommended. For seniors just starting the serious college admissions race, school exam-style questions will still be more familiar than CSAT-style questions. Therefore, without prior exposure to CSAT-style questions, you might panic the moment you see the test paper. So, through past CSAT, Academic Assessment, and mock evaluation questions within the scope of the last three years, you need to understand how concepts are applied in problems and train yourself to become familiar with new question types. (개념정리가 어느 정도 됐다면 최근 3년간의 기출문제를 푸는 것을 추천한다. 이제 막 본격적인 대입 레이스에 참가하는 고3 학생들에게는 아직까지 수능형 문제보다는 내신형 문제가 더 익숙할 것이다. 그렇기에 수능형 문제를 미리 경험해보지 않으면 시험지를 받아 보는 순간 당황할 수 있다. 따라서 최근 3년간의 출제범위 내 수능, 학력평가, 모의평가의 기출문제를 통해 개념이 문제에서 어떻게 활용되는지 파악하고, 새로운 문제 유형 등에 익숙해지는 훈련을 할 필요가 있다.)

Use it as a Compass for Admission Success through the 'Susijeong' (Rolling Admission) Track (수시 전형 합격 위한 나침반 활용)

Retakers (N-suseng) do not take the March Academic Assessment, and some elective subjects in the Mathematics section are partially excluded from the question scope. Also, with much time remaining until the CSAT, it has limitations as a test to accurately determine your objective position. Nevertheless, it is necessary to do a mid-point check by comparing your scores from the Academic Assessment with your grades 1 and 2 school records, assessing which admission track is advantageous for applying to your desired universities. (3월 학평은 N수생들이 응시하지 않고, 수학 영역에서 선택 과목의 출제 범위도 일부 제외된다. 또한, 수능까지 아직 많은 시간이 남아 있어 자신의 객관적인 위치를 정확히 파악할 수 있는 시험이라고 보기에는 한계가 있다. 그럼에도 학평에서 얻은 자신의 점수와 1, 2학년 학생부 교과 성적을 비교해보면서 희망 대학을 지원하기 위해 어떤 전형이 유리한지 중간 점검을 해볼 필요는 있다.)

Woo Yeon-cheol said, "If your regular school grades tend to be better than your Academic Assessment scores, it's better to focus more on preparing for the midterm and final exams in the first semester of your senior year. If the school records-based admission track at your target university applies a CSAT minimum score requirement, you should not neglect managing your CSAT grade levels by subject to meet the requirement." (우연철 소장은 “평소 교과 성적이 학평 성적보다 잘 나오는 경우라면 3학년 1학기 중간·기말 고사 대비에 좀더 집중하는 것이 좋다”며 “만약 지원하려는 대학의 학생부 교과전형이 수능 최저학력기준을 적용하고 있다면 기준 충족을 위해 수능 영역별 등급 관리 또한 소홀히 해서는 안 된다”고 말했다.)

Kim Byung-jin, head of the Etoos Education Assessment Research Institute, advised, "You need to utilize the Academic Assessment focusing on the completeness of your learning during the winter vacation. For example, establish a study plan based mainly on questions you thought you had studied enough for but got wrong in practice. Furthermore, if you have the rolling admission (Susijeong) CSAT minimum score standards in mind, setting the required grade level for each subject and checking how many more correct answers you need, then establishing your future study plan, is also a good method." (김병진 이투스 교육평가연구소장은 “겨울 방학 동안 학습했던 내용의 학습 완성도를 중심으로 학력평가를 활용할 필요가 있다. 일례로 학습을 충분히 했다고 생각했으나 실전에서 틀리는 문제를 중심으로 이후의 학습 계획을 수립해야 한다”며 “나아가 수시 수능최저학력기준을 염두에 두고 있는 경우 영역별 필요 등급을 설정해 두고 몇 문제가 더 필요한지를 살펴 이후 학습 계획을 수립하는 것도 좋은 방법”이라고 조언했다.)

If your CSAT competitiveness is lacking, you should establish a support strategy to actively utilize other admission factors such as essays or practical tests. (만약, 수능 경쟁력이 부족한 학생이라면 논술, 실기 등 다른 전형요소를 적극 활용할 수 있도록 지원 전략을 수립해야 한다.)

Establish a Phase-by-Phase Study Plan Until the CSAT (수능 때까지 시기별 학습계획 세워야)

The most important thing is to identify your weak subjects based on the subject-specific results of the March Academic Assessment, consider ways to supplement them, and concretely set long-term goals and plans for improving your CSAT scores. Rather than obsessing over the test results, use this as a stepping stone for a new start by objectively identifying your skills and weaknesses. Even if your scores differ from expectations, adopt the mindset of gaining practical experience, set your target CSAT score and grade level, and use this as foundational data for establishing your CSAT subject-wise study plans and designing your college admission preparation direction for the remaining period. (가장 중요한 건 3월 학평 과목별 결과를 토대로 취약과목을 파악, 이를 보완할 방법을 고민하는 한편 수능 성적 향상을 위한 장기 목표와 계획을 구체적으로 설정하는 것이다. 시험 결과에 연연하기보다는 자신의 실력과 취약점을 객관적으로 파악하는 등 새로운 출발을 하는 디딤돌로 삼아야 한다. 성적이 기대와 다르게 나왔다 하더라도 실전 경험을 쌓는다는 생각을 갖고 수능 목표 점수와 등급을 정하고 남은 기간 수능 영역별 학습 계획을 세우는 근거 자료와 입시 준비 방향을 설계하는 기초 자료로 활용해야 한다.)

Woo Yeon-cheol stated, "If your Academic Assessment scores are higher than your efforts warrant, rather than feeling overly confident, you should check whether you solved problems with a thorough understanding of concepts and accurately grasped the test maker's intent. Only then can you minimize mistakes on the actual CSAT." (우연철 소장은 “학평 성적이 자신의 노력에 비해 높게 나왔을 경우 의기양양해하기보다는 완벽한 개념 이해와 더불어 출제 의도를 정확하게 알고 풀었던 것인지 체크하고 넘어가야 실제 수능에서 실수를 최소화할 수 있다”고 말했다.)

Unfortunately, if your scores are lower than expected, the priority is to clearly identify the reasons for your incorrect answers. Instead of being impatient, adopt the mindset that you will gradually reduce mistakes before the CSAT through concept organization, and focus on establishing study strategies and plans for the upcoming mock exams and the CSAT. (안타깝게도 자신이 예상했던 것보다 성적이 잘 나오지 않은 학생이라면 틀린 문제의 원인을 명확히 파악하는 것이 우선이다. 조급한 마음보다는 개념 정리를 통해 수능 전까지 실수를 점차 줄여나가겠다는 생각을 가지고 앞으로 몇 차례 더 치르게 될 모의고사와 수능에 초점을 맞춰 학습 전략과 계획을 세울 필요가 있다.)

Kim Byung-jin advised, "Even if it's tough, be sure to review the entire test process and all subject questions on the day of the exam, analyzing the overall question patterns, high-scoring questions, and incorrect answers. In particular, instead of just checking the correct answers for wrong questions, you should detail the reasons for mistakes, accurate problem-solving methods, the question's scope, and related concepts, reviewing them periodically." (김병진 소장은 “힘들더라도 반드시 시험이 끝난 당일 시험 과정, 전 과목 문제를 복기하며 전반적인 출제 유형, 고득점 문항, 오답 분석을 해야 한다”며 “특히 틀린 문제는 단순히 정답만 확인하는 것이 아니라 틀린 이유와 정확한 문제풀이 방법, 문항 출제 범위 및 관련 개념 등을 상세히 정리해 수시로 확인하는 것이 좋다”고 조언했다.)

If you haven't yet met the CSAT minimum score requirements of your desired universities, or if your Academic Assessment scores are generally better than your school records and you are considering the regular admissions (Jeongsi) track as your main focus, the Academic Assessment and subsequent mock evaluations are truly stepping-stone opportunities to raise your grades. Based on the subject-specific results, you must concretely set long-term goals and plans for improving CSAT scores, such as identifying your weak subjects and considering how to supplement them. (희망 대학에서 요구하는 수능 최저학력기준을 아직 충족하지 못했거나 학생부 교과 성적보다 학평 성적이 대체로 더 잘 나와 정시를 주력 전형으로 고려하고 있는 수험생이라면 학평과 이후 모의평가는 그야말로 등급을 올릴 수 있는 디딤돌 같은 기회다. 과목별 결과를 토대로 자신의 취약과목을 파악하고 앞으로 어떻게 보완할지 고민하는 등 수능 성적 향상을 위한 장기 목표와 계획을 구체적으로 설정해야 한다.)

Lee Chi-woo, head of Visang Education Admissions Assessment Center, said, "Set your target CSAT score and grade level, and use this as foundational data for creating your study plans for each CSAT subject area during the remaining period." He emphasized the importance of checking how much you need to improve to gain admission to your target university and establishing a phase-by-phase study plan until the CSAT based on your results by area and subject. (이치우 비상교육 입시평가연구소장은 “수능 목표 점수와 등급을 정하고, 남은 기간 수능 영역별 학습 계획을 세우기 위한 근거 자료로 활용해야 한다”고 말했다. 자신이 목표로 한 대학에 입학하기 위해 어느 정도까지 성적을 향상해야 하는지 점검하고, 영역·과목별 성적 결과를 바탕으로 수능 때까지 시기별 학습계획을 세우는 것이 중요하다는 것이다.)

Preparation Considering the CSAT Subject Reflection of Desired Universities (희망 대학 수능 반영(과목) 영역 대비)

Establishing a long-term strategic study plan, starting from the March Academic Assessment until the CSAT on November 19th, is paramount. During the first semester, study focusing on the subject areas reflected by your desired universities, carefully checking which areas are weighted and adjusting your study emphasis accordingly. It helps to set and implement specific daily or weekly study plans by area and subject. Using Academic Assessment and CSAT mock exam workbooks, identify weak units and assessment areas for each subject/area, then select one suitable self-study or reference book per subject alongside the EBS CSAT textbook, and recommend studying each at least twice. (3월 학평을 시작으로 오는 11월19일 수능시험까지 장기간 전략적인 공부 계획을 세우는 것이 무엇보다 중요하다. 1학기 동안에는 희망 대학 수능 반영 영역(과목)을 중심으로 공부하되, 가중치 부여 영역(과목) 등을 꼼꼼히 챙겨 공부 비중을 달리할 필요가 있다. 영역·과목별로 구체적인 일일 또는 주간 학습계획을 세워 실천하는 것이 도움이 된다. 학평과 수능 모의평가 문제집 등을 통해 영역(과목)별 부족한 단원과 평가 영역 등을 파악한 뒤 영역(과목)별로 EBS 수능특강 교재와 함께 자신에게 맞는 자습서 또는 참고서를 1권씩 선정해 최소 2회 정도 반복 학습하는 것을 추천한다.)

Woo Yeon-cheol advised, "Based on the subject-specific results of the March Academic Assessment, you must identify your weak subjects, consider how to improve them, and set concrete long-term goals and plans for improving your CSAT scores. After taking the mock exam, analyze the reasons for your incorrect answers, re-solve the wrong problems, and if you don't understand something, actively refer to your textbooks. Especially if you have many wrong answers, you need to strengthen your foundation by re-learning concepts from the beginning, rather than just solving problems." (우연철 소장은 “3월 학평 과목별 결과를 토대로 자신의 취약과목을 파악하고 앞으로 어떻게 보완할지 고민하는 등 수능 성적 향상을 위한 장기 목표와 계획을 구체적으로 설정해야 한다”며 “모의고사를 본 이후에는 오답의 원인을 분석해 틀린 문제는 다시 풀어보고, 이해가 되지 않는다면 교과서 등을 적극 참고해야 한다. 특히 오답이 많다면 문제풀이만 할 것이 아니라 개념 이해부터 다시 학습하는 등 기초를 다질 필요가 있다”고 조언했다.)

In this regard, Lee Man-gi, head of the Uway Education Assessment Research Institute, suggested the following subject-specific study strategies until the CSAT: "For Korean Language, focus on improving reading comprehension, but before that, accurate understanding of the beginning of passages or sentences and the answer choices is necessary. For Mathematics, concentrate on weak units or question types, but when solving problems, check if any concepts were missed. For English, rather than solving many problems from March, use past exam questions to identify wrong answers in high-difficulty types and avoid repeating the same mistakes. For Inquiry subjects, basic principles from EBS CSAT textbooks are important, but figures, photos, diagrams, etc., are also highly likely to be presented similarly, so you should study them carefully." (이와 관련해 이만기 유웨이 교육평가연구소장은 수능 때까지 과목별 학습 전략을 다음과 같이 제안했다. “국어는 본문 독해력을 키우는 데 주력하되, 그 전에 글이나 문장의 첫머리, 답지에 대한 정확한 이해가 필요하다. 수학은 취약단원이나 유형을 집중적으로 공부하되, 문제를 풀 때는 놓친 개념이 있는지 확인해야 한다. 영어는 3월부터 많은 문제를 풀기보다는 기출문제를 이용해 난도 높은 유형에서의 오답을 확인하고 같은 실수를 반복하지 않도록 해야 한다. 탐구는 EBS 수능교재에 나와 있는 기본 원리뿐 아니라 그림, 사진, 도표 등 자료 또한 유사하게 출제될 가능성이 높으므로 이를 잘 봐야 한다.”)

Meanwhile, the Academic Assessments administered by the municipal and provincial education offices this year will be held four times in total: March 24th, followed by May 7th (Gyeonggi Provincial Office of Education), July 8th (Incheon Metropolitan Office of Education), and October 20th (Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education). The mock evaluations administered by KICE, the CSAT organizer, are held twice – on June 4th and September 2nd. Since both current seniors and graduates take these, they offer the most accurate prediction of your scores on the actual CSAT, which will be held on November 19th. (한편, 올해 시도교육청이 주관하는 학평은 3월24일에 이어 5월7일(경기도교육청), 7월8일(인천시교육청), 10월20일(서울시교육청) 등 총 4번 실시된다. 수능을 주관하는 한국교육과정평가원에서 시행하는 모의평가는 6월4일과 9월2일 두 번 치러지는데, 고3 수험생은 물론 졸업생도 함께 치르기 때문에 11월19일 치러질 실제 수능에서 본인의 성적을 가장 정확하게 예측해볼 수 있다.)

Reporter Kim Mi-young kimmy@hani.co.kr (김미영 기자 kimmy@hani.co.kr)

item.title: "Shall We Look for Green Seasonal Ingredients Today?" (“오늘은 초록색 제철 재료를 찾아볼까”)
item.description:
"In-season core" is trending. It refers to a lifestyle of seeking out and eating foods that are in season, making a point to go out and see flowers that bloom for a season, and enjoying activities that align with the 24 solar terms. This trend, which has spread among the young generation in their 20s and 30s, is actually even more crucial for children. Kids growing up in supermarkets where strawberries are sold year-round and indoor lifestyles that run regardless of the weather are likely to learn about seasonal changes with their heads rather than their bodies. That's why experiencing seasonal foods and solar terms firsthand and feeling them on their skin is all the more necessary. Here, we introduce know-how for teaching solar terms in everyday life that awakens children's seasonal sensibility. <<> Learning the Sense of Seasons Through Taste <<> The easiest and most powerful solar term education begins at the dining table. Rather than big-box supermarkets, try visiting traditional markets or local food direct-sale stores with your child. In spring, smelling the slightly bitter flavor of shepherd's purse and wild chives with the tip of your nose, and in summer, touching the deep green young plums with your hands — these experiences themselves are living lessons. <<> When you go to the market, don't just stop at shopping—give your child a small mission. Try missions based on colors, like "Today, let's find a yellow seasonal ingredient," or have them ask a vendor elder the name of a vegetable they've never seen before. Through brief conversations with unfamiliar adults, children can naturally gain vivid information about seasonal foods along with valuable social experiences. <<> Putting foods that match the solar terms on the table is also a good method. On Daeboreum (the first full moon), eat ogokbap (five-grain rice) and namul (seasoned greens) together while cracking nuts, and on Dongji (winter solstice), boil red bean porridge while having a conversation like, "They say today is the longest night of the year—why do you think that is?" Even without grand explanations, a short conversation shared around the dinner table is the most natural education that makes solar terms memorable for a long time. <<> Involving your child in the cooking process is also great. In spring, make jam while picking strawberry stems or make spring cabbage bibimbap; in summer, cut watermelon to make fruit punch (hwache); in autumn, peel persimmons, hang them under the eaves, and observe the process of them becoming dried persimmons. In winter, gather the whole family to make kimchi or soak red beans and boil red bean porridge. Through tastes and activities that change with each season, you can naturally awaken a sense of the seasons. <<> Fun Solar Term Activities to Enjoy in Everyday Life <<> Solar terms were once the standard of an agrarian society, but for modern children, they can become the standard of delightful seasonal play. For example, on Ipchun (February 4), which marks the beginning of spring, you can write "Ipchun-daegil" (立春大吉, wishing good fortune for the year) in Chinese characters or color it in and post it at home. The upcoming Gogu (April 20) is the solar term when spring rain falls and nourishes all grains. As the full-fledged farming season begins, plant seeds in a pot and start a seed growth journal. You can record in drawings what seeds were planted and when and how much water was given. <<> In summer, there are Haji and Daeseo. Haji (June 21) is the longest day of the year. On this day, stick a stick into the ground with your child, measure the length of its shadow, and record it in the morning, at noon, and in the evening. You can create a fascinating science session where you directly observe the sun's position changing with your own eyes. Daeseo (July 23) is the hottest period. Share stories of how ancestors ate samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup) and soaked their feet in streams to fend off the heat, then make and enjoy seasonal foods like cool watermelon punch or cucumber cold soup together. On Chubun (September 23), record the time the sun sets together, and afterward, observe the sunset time each day to experience the days growing shorter. The fact that this is a day when day and night are in balance becomes an amazing discovery for a child. <<> Observing solar terms in this way is, in itself, a small event that makes everyday life richer. If you step away from the perspective of education and turn it into a family activity of joyfully celebrating the seasons, your child will come to look forward to and observe solar terms with anticipation and curiosity. <<> Cultivating Seasonal Sensibility Through Reading and Recording <<> Adding picture books to solar term activities connects experiences to language. "Solar Term Magic" (text by Cheon Mi-jin, illustrations by Min Seung-ji) is a picture book that warmly unfolds the 24 solar terms through the four-season story of a family that moves to a countryside home. It teaches children, at their eye level, that solar terms are not grand concepts but a joyful rhythm that enriches daily life. "The 24 Solar Terms Picture Book at a Glance" (text by Ji Ho-jin, illustrations by Lee Hyeok) weaves the 24 solar terms from Ipchun to Daehan into engaging stories and illustrations. It includes the meanings and origins behind each solar term's name, natural phenomena that appear during those periods, and the wisdom of ancestors in applying solar terms to farming and daily life. <<> Adding record-keeping to reading deepens seasonal sensibility even further. Pick a walking path in your neighborhood with your child, and each time the solar terms change, take photos in the same spot or record changes in colors and smells. Choose a tree near home that you like and observe it throughout the entire year. As you record the process of leaves sprouting, flowers blooming, leaves turning autumn colors, and branches being left bare, it becomes a more vivid natural textbook than any science book after a year. If your child is still unfamiliar with writing, simply drawing with colors and shapes is more than enough. <<> If you want to start a bit more lightly, hanging a calendar on the wall featuring the 24 solar terms or seasonal foods for each season is also a good idea. When your child starts to look at the calendar first and asks, "What's the next solar term? What do we eat then?" solar term education is already half successful. If you want to go one step further, make a "season box" with your child. It's an activity of preparing a small box for each season and collecting natural objects that can only be found during that time. In the spring box, press-dried cherry blossom petals or sprout seeds; in the summer box, seashells picked up at the beach or cicada shells; in the autumn box, acorns and autumn leaves; and in the winter box, dried tangerine peels. <<> Solar term education is not about memorization but about experiences in daily life. It's okay not to know the names of the solar terms. A conversation that begins with a simple remark like, "Don't you think the air is starting to smell like spring?" or "The days are getting longer than last month, aren't they?" awakens a child's seasonal sensibility. Choose one activity per season to make everyday life a little richer. After spending a year that way, before you know it, your child will have grown into someone who can say first, "I think summer is coming soon." <<> Park Eun-ah, Contributing Writer (‘제철 코어'가 유행이다. 그 계절에 나는 음식을 찾아 먹고, 한철 피는 꽃을 보러 일부러 길을 나서고, 24기 절기에 맞는 활동을 즐기는 삶의 방식을 뜻한다. 2030 젊은 세대 사이에서 번진 이 유행은 사실 아이들에게 더 절실하다. 사계절 내내 딸기가 팔리는 마트, 날씨와 무관하게 돌아가는 실내 생활 속에서 자라는 아이들은 계절의 변화를 몸이 아닌 머리로 배우기 쉽다. 제철과 절기를 직접 맛보고 피부로 느끼는 경험이 더욱 필요한 이유다. 아이의 계절 감수성을 깨우는 일상 속 절기 교육 노하우를 소개한다.)

item.title: Deepening Historical Curiosity Sparked by 'The King and the Clown' (‘왕과 사는 남자’로 깊어진 역사 호기심 더 키워볼까)
item.description:
The box office success of the film 'The King and the Clown' sparked an unexpected phenomenon. Audiences leaving theaters began heading to Yeongwol, Gangwon Province. Cheongnyeongpo, where King Danjong was exiled, and Jangneung Royal Tomb saw far more visitors than usual, and search queries about the real history of Danjong and Eom Heung-do surged. A single historical film or comic book can serve as a more powerful and engaging history teacher than any textbook. From historical content worth watching with children to ways of connecting it with historical tours, here is a collection of history education methods you can try in everyday life. <<> Encountering History Through Film and Drama Stories <<> Among films and dramas, there is an endless array of works set against real history. Simply watching such works tailored to a child's age or school curriculum provides excellent indirect experience. The moment a figure reduced to a single line in a textbook comes alive on screen, history approaches in an entirely different way. <<> For young children and elementary schoolers, the animated series 'K-Pop Demon Hunters,' which enjoyed explosive popularity last year, is a great starting point. Set in the modern day, this work follows K-pop girl group Huntrix as secret demon hunters protecting the world, but it is steeped in Korean traditional culture throughout. While watching, look for elements of Korean folk belief such as the afterlife messenger, dokkaebi (goblins), and the magpie tiger, along with traditional symbols like hanbok, hanok, and Seoul landmarks. Asking questions like "What's the name of that weapon that character is holding?" or "Doesn't that building look familiar?" and searching for answers together is already the beginning of fascinating history study. <<> For upper elementary students and above, you can seek out content that delves deeper into history. For example, the film 'The Throne' portrays the story of King Yeongjo and Crown Prince Sado with a focus on the characters' perspectives, making it ideal for examining the human emotions and dilemmas behind historical events. There are also many other films dealing with major historical events or figures, such as 'The Admiral: Roaring Currents' about the naval battles of the Imjin War, 'Astronomy: Ask the Sky' about King Sejong and Jang Yeong-sil, 'The Fortress' set during the Byeongja Horan, and 'Dongju: The Portrait of a Poet,' which depicts the Japanese colonial period through the story of poet Yun Dong-ju. (영화 ‘왕과 사는 남자’가 흥행하면서 뜻밖의 현상이 일어났다. 극장을 나온 관객들이 강원도 영월로 향하기 시작한 것이다. 단종이 유배됐던 청령포와 장릉에는 평소보다 훨씬 많은 방문객이 찾았고, 단종과 엄흥도의 실제 역사를 찾아보는 검색량도 치솟았다. 역사를 다룬 영화 한 편, 만화책 한 권이 어떤 교과서보다 강력하고 흥미로운 역사 선생님이 될 수 있다. 아이와 함께 볼 만한 역사 콘텐츠부터 역사 기행과 연결하는 방법까지, 일상에서 시도해볼 수 있는 역사 교육 방법을 모아 봤다.)

After watching content, looking up additional information about the characters can deepen the lasting impression. It's also important to explore together where historical facts and cinematic imagination diverge. Especially from upper elementary grades onward, children begin to develop the cognitive ability to distinguish between dramatic portrayal and actual fact, so it's advisable to pair this with media literacy training that encourages critical consumption of content. (영화와 드라마 이야기로 접하는 역사)

For children of the video generation, YouTube is also a highly accessible learning tool. The key is choosing the right channel. EBS's 'History Channel e' is a program that stylishly reconstructs major scenes or events in Korean history in short episodes of around five minutes each. It's well-suited to children's attention spans, and episodes can be searched by topic on the EBS website and YouTube channel. Dasan Books' culture channel 'Gyoyang Mandu' tackles intriguing historical questions like "How did Joseon kings use the bathroom?" with charming illustrations and humor, making it a light and fun way to approach history. <<> Starting History Study Through the Joy of Reading <<> When studying history, the most familiar entry point is, of course, books. For children who find history difficult or are very young, starting with comic books is a good approach. In the early grades when children first encounter history, it's better to focus on gripping stories centered on specific figures or events rather than chronological learning. <<> 'Yongseonsaeng's Lively Korean History' (Sahoepyeongnon) is a series that has long held its place as essential reading for history learning. Using a storytelling format where the character Yongseonsaeng roams historical sites with children, it allows readers to naturally follow the long arc from prehistoric times to the modern era as if it were a story. The authors personally visited over 200 cultural heritage sites across 37 major cities nationwide, and on-site lectures highlighting the key points can also be viewed via QR code videos. <<> Once a child starts showing interest in history comics, books like 'Seol Min-seok's Korean History Grand Adventure' (Dankkumai) are also a great choice. There's an animated version based on the same content, so books and videos can be used together. <<> For middle schoolers and older, reading historical novels together and discussing them can be rewarding. A notable example worth trying is Han Kang's 'Human Acts' (Changbi), which won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Literature. Set against the May 18 Gwangju Democratization Movement, the novel vividly portrays the figures who fought against martial law forces and the stories of those left behind. It allows readers to experience tragic modern history not as a mere textbook event but as the stories of living people. After reading, visiting Gwangju's National May 18 Memorial Cemetery or the May 18 Archives together connects the book's stories to living history. <<> Author Lee Geum-yi's 'Aloha, My Mothers' is set in Hawaii during the Japanese colonial period and tells the stories of first-generation overseas Koreans and the women who married them and built their lives there. The author, beloved as a leading figure in young adult literature, weaves historical facts into warm character-driven narratives. <<> Historical Outings Connected to Content <<> Interest sparked by content becomes more deeply ingrained when it connects to historical sites. After watching a drama or film, a simple remark like "That scene's backdrop is a real place—should we go see it?" creates exciting motivation for a child. For example, after watching 'The Fortress,' walk the trails of Namhansanseong Fortress, or after 'A Resistance,' visit Seodaemun Prison History Hall. When content and sites are linked this way, a child recalls scenes from the film at every stone wall or exhibit, absorbing history with a completely different depth. <<> When you arrive at the site, it's important not to leave the child as a passive observer. Before visiting a historical location featured in a film, set a mission together with your child. Simple missions like "Find the spot that most resembles the scene from the movie" or "Spot objects in the exhibits that appeared in the drama" turn a potentially boring visit into an exciting adventure. For a more active approach, try a 'day curator' activity where the child becomes the guide and explains the site to the guardian. Look up related information together in advance, and let the child explain on-site—this builds both a sense of accomplishment and learning effectiveness. <<> Among the most accessible historical sites, Seoul's Gyeongbokgung Palace and Changdeokgung Palace are unmissable. These two palaces, backdrops to countless historical dramas, can naturally be visited after watching any Joseon-era drama or film. If you've just watched content about the independence movement, head to Seodaemun Prison History Hall or the An Jung-geun Memorial Museum on Namsan. <<> History Education Methods You Can Use at Home Right Away <<> The best way to leverage content in history education is simpler than you might think. After a film or drama ends, asking just one question is enough. A light question like "Which character stood out to you most today?" or "What kind of life do you think you'd have lived if you were born in that era?" plants the seed of historical imagination in a child's mind. Guardians don't need to feel pressured to know all the historical facts themselves. What matters more is the attitude of being curious and searching together. <<> After viewing content, activities that follow immediately while emotions are still fresh are most effective. Try writing a brief reflection as a drawing or short essay after watching. If writing is difficult, simply prompting a verbal response like "What would you say to one of the characters you saw today?" is more than enough. <<> There's one essential thing to keep in mind: historical dramas and films mix historical facts with fiction. To keep a child from taking everything in a drama as 100% fact, cultivate the habit after watching of exploring together, asking, "Is this scene real history, or a story the writer imagined?" Clearly pointing out, "Dramas add imagination for entertainment, but the actual records say this," is enough for a child to naturally learn to critically accept information. Over time, this process nurtures not only historical knowledge but also a critical eye toward media. <<> Park Eun-ah, Contributing Reporter (영화와 드라마 중에는 실제 역사를 배경으로 한 작품이 무궁무진하다. 이런 작품을 아이의 연령대나 교과 과정에 맞춰 보는 것만으로도 훌륭한 간접 체험이 된다. 교과서에서 한 줄로 처리된 인물이 영화 속에서 살아 숨 쉬는 존재가 되는 순간, 역사는 전혀 다르게 다가온다.)

]]>

item.title: "Fostering 'AI Leaders with Virtue'" (“‘덕성(德性) 갖춘 AI 리더’ 길러내겠다”)
item.description:
What kind of talent is needed in an era where artificial intelligence (AI) finds the answers? As AI reshapes the order of society as a whole, corporate hiring standards are also changing. While academic background and knowledge have been the deciding factors until now, there is a view that in the AI era, communication skills—the ability to think and collaborate alongside machines—will become increasingly important. With the advent of AI, rather than talent built on rote memorization, individuals who freely express their thoughts and perspectives while valuing morality, ethics, and the public good are expected to rise in prominence. (인공지능(AI)이 답을 찾아주는 시대에는 어떤 인재가 필요할까. 인공지능이 사회 전반의 질서를 재편하면서 기업의 인재 채용 기준도 변화하고 있다. 지금까지는 학력과 지식이 좌우했다면, AI 시대의 인재는 기계와 함께 생각하고 협력하는 소통능력이 중요해질 것이라는 의견이 나온다. 인공지능의 등장으로, 많이 외워 만들어진 인재보다는 학생들의 생각과 관점을 자유롭게 표현하되 도덕과 윤리, 공공성을 중시하는 인재가 각광받을 것이라는 의미다.)

This is why Duksung Women's University President Min Jae-hong emphasized upon taking office in February, "AI and digital transformation are already a reality," adding, "We will build an AI-based university where technological efficiency and human values strike a balance—one that reflects together on 'ethics, publicness, responsibility, and human dignity.'" (민재홍 덕성여대 총장이 지난 2월 취임하면서 “AI·디지털 전환은 이미 현실이 됐다”며 “기술의 효율성과 인간의 가치가 균형을 이루는, 즉 ‘윤리·공공성·책임성·인간의 존엄성’을 함께 성찰하는 AI 기반 대학으로 만들겠다”고 강조한 이유다.)

In this regard, President Min has set Duksung's direction as "X+AI" rather than "AI+X." This means AI is not the master; rather, each major (X) remains the core, and AI serves as the wings that expand the capabilities of that major. This philosophy extends the spirit of self-reliance, self-sufficiency, and self-awareness of the university's founder, Cha Mi-ri-sa, to fit the AI era, and is designed to lead to the cultivation of "virtuous AI leaders." (이와 관련해 민 총장은 덕성의 방향을 ‘AI+X’보다 ‘X+AI’로 설정했다. AI가 주인이 아니라 각 전공(X)이 중심이고, AI는 그 전공의 역량을 확장하는 날개가 되어야 한다는 뜻이다. 이 철학은 설립자인 차미리사 선생의 자생·자립·자각 정신을 AI 시대에 맞게 확장한 것으로 ‘덕성(德性) AI 리더’ 양성으로 이어지도록 설계한 것이다.)

We spoke with President Min Jae-hong about the direction Duksung Women's University should take in these rapidly changing times, its goals and philosophy for talent development, and his aspirations as president. (민재홍 총장에게 급변하는 시대에 덕성여대가 나아가야 할 방향과 인재양성 목표와 철학, 총장으로서의 포부 등을 들어봤다.)

–It has been just over a month since you took office as the 13th president. What are your thoughts? (–13대 총장으로 취임한 지 한 달 남짓 지났다. 소감은.)

"The past month has been a time of 'review,' not 'ceremony.' Since taking office, I moved quickly to identify where Duksung's education, research, and administration are stuck and where students feel inconveniences, and I am preparing to implement the promises I made. Above all, since we are in a digital revolution era where AI is the dominant trend, I intend to prioritize the reorganization of the educational system. Through the establishment of an AI-based customized platform that connects everything from 'course registration—grades—campus life—counseling—employment and career' into one integrated system, and the development of courses and curricula where AI is integrated into every major, I will achieve educational innovation that students can feel, leading to employment outcomes." (“지난 한 달은 ‘인사’의 시간이 아니라 ‘점검’의 시간이었다. 취임 이후 덕성의 교육·연구·행정이 어떤 지점에서 막히고, 학생들이 어디에서 불편을 체감하는지부터 빠르게 확인했고, 공약했던 내용들을 실행하기 위한 준비를 하고 있다. 무엇보다 AI가 대세가 된 디지털 혁명시대인 만큼 교육체계 개편을 우선적으로 실행하려고 한다. ‘수강신청-성적-학교생활-상담-취업·진로’까지 하나로 연결되는 AI 기반 맞춤형 플랫폼 구축, 모든 전공에 AI가 접목되는 교과목 및 커리큘럼 개발을 통해 학생들이 체감하는 교육혁신을 이뤄내, 취업으로 연결될 수 있게 하겠다.”)

–You have said you will transform Duksung Women's University into a university that cultivates new innovative talent, like prestigious women's colleges Wellesley College and Smith College. In this regard, you have emphasized the 'Duksung AI Initiative.' What is its core? (–총장께서는 덕성여대를 여성 명문 대학인 웰즐리 칼리지(Wellesley College), 스미스 칼리지(Smith College)처럼 새로운 혁신의 인재를 길러내는 대학으로 만들겠다고 했다. 이와 관련해 ‘덕성 AI 이니셔티브’를 강조했는데, 핵심은.)

"The 'Duksung AI Initiative' is a transformation into an AI-based university where technological efficiency and human values are balanced. We will introduce AI across education, research, and administration while simultaneously promoting reflection on ethics, publicness, responsibility, and human dignity. Duksung's AI transformation must be human-centered, not technology-centered. By building an AI-era education where majors are not excluded and human intelligence is not marginalized, we will develop into a sustainable future-oriented university where all members grow together." (“‘덕성 AI 이니셔티브’는 기술 효율성과 인간 가치가 균형을 이루는 AI 기반 대학 전환이다. AI를 교육·연구·행정 전반에 도입하고, 동시에 윤리·공공성·책임성, 인간 존엄성에 대한 성찰도 함께 추진하겠다. 덕성의 AI 전환은 기술 중심이 아니라 사람 중심이어야 한다. 전공이 배제되지 않고 인간의 지능이 소외되지 않는 AI 시대 교육을 구축해 모든 구성원이 함께 성장하는 지속가능한 미래형 대학으로 발전시켜나가겠다.”)

–As a women's university, what is Duksung's role in the AI era? (–여성대학으로서 AI 시대에 ‘덕성’의 역할은.)

"In the AI era, I believe universities must go beyond simply 'teaching technology' and also cultivate the judgment—ethics, publicness, and critical thinking—needed to use technology responsibly. Based on our identity as an 'educational community that converts women's potential into social value,' I believe Duksung's role is to nurture the women leaders essential in the AI era—those equipped with ethics, publicness, and critical thinking—and that this is the path to realizing a 'distinguished Duksung.'" (“AI 시대 대학은 단순히 기술을 ‘가르치는 곳’을 넘어, 기술을 책임 있게 활용할 수 있는 판단력(윤리·공공성·비판적 사고)을 함께 길러야 한다고 생각한다. ‘여성의 잠재력을 사회적 가치로 전환시키는 교육 공동체’라는 정체성을 바탕으로, 윤리·공공성·비판적 사고를 갖춘 AI 시대에 꼭 필요한 여성 리더를 길러내는 것이 덕성의 역할이자, ‘명문 덕성’을 구현해내는 길이라고 생각한다. ”)

–If you were to describe the talent Duksung aims to cultivate in one sentence? (–덕성이 길러내고자 하는 인재를 한 문장으로 말한다면.)

"'AI leaders with virtue.' Not people who are merely 'good at using technology,' but people who can read the limitations and biases of technology and judge social responsibility alongside it. In other words, creative, convergent AI talent equipped with humanities and social imagination, scientific and technological creativity, and artistic and cultural sensibility." (“‘덕성(德性)을 갖춘 AI 리더’다. 기술을 ‘잘 쓰는 사람’이 아니라, 기술의 한계·편향을 읽고 사회적 책임을 함께 판단하는 사람이다. 즉, 인문사회학적 상상력, 과학기술 창조력, 예술문화 감각을 갖춘 창의융합형 AI 인재다.”)

–What are the specific action plans for cultivating 'AI leaders with virtue'? (–‘덕성 갖춘 AI 리더’ 양성을 위한 구체적인 실천방안은.)

"It's not about 'AI for select advanced departments only,' but rather 'building basic competencies for all students + in-depth competencies by major + an educational support system.' To this end, we will make AI basic competency mandatory for all students (evolving from 'computational thinking' to 'Duksung AI literacy'), have the 'AI Convergence Education Support Center' provide standardized AI-Wing lecture plans and practice materials ('meal kits'), match AI TAs, and even support students' AI subscriptions (e.g., paid ChatGPT versions/credits). In short, it can be summarized as: △Making AI literacy mandatory for all students △Expanding X+AI courses across majors △Establishing AI-Wing (standard lecture plans/practice) and AI TA systems △Industry-academia linked projects (e.g., AI drug discovery and bio-health clusters)." (“‘특정 첨단학과만의 AI’가 아니라, ‘전교생 기본 역량 + 전공별 심화 역량 + 교육지원 체계를 구축’하는 것이다. 이를 위해 전교생 AI 기초 역량을 필수화하고(‘컴퓨팅사고’ → ‘덕성 AI 리터러시’), ‘AI 융합교육 지원센터’에서 표준화된 AI-Wing 강의안·실습자료(‘밀키트’) 제공, AI TA 매칭, 학생들의 AI 구독(예: ChatGPT 유료 버전/크레딧) 지원까지 연결할 것이다. 간단히 말하면, △전교생 AI 리터러시 필수화 △전공별 X+AI 교과 확대 △AI-Wing(표준 강의안·실습)과 AI TA 체계 △산학 연계형 프로젝트(예: AI 신약·바이오헬스 클러스터 등) 등으로 요약할 수 있겠다.”)

–What are Duksung Women's University's unique strengths, and how do you plan to develop them? (–덕성여대만의 강점은 무엇이고, 이를 어떻게 키워나갈 계획인지.)

"People often mistakenly think of women's universities as being primarily focused on humanities and social sciences. But our university has various humanities and social science majors such as early childhood education, art history, and cultural anthropology, as well as science and technology-related majors including five tracks within digital software engineering, bioengineering, food and nutrition, chemistry, and information statistics. Furthermore, the Future Talent College houses 'cutting-edge' departments such as AI Drug Discovery, Data Science, and Virtual Reality Convergence. In other words, our strength lies in not concentrating 'advanced' fields in specific departments, but in having a structure where entire major groups—science and technology, data, content, bio—share AI as a basic competency. To support this, we will establish an 'AI Convergence Education Support Center' to provide AI-Wing lecture plans, practice templates, and assessment standards that can be immediately applied to major courses, match AI TAs, and support student AI subscriptions, thereby raising the quality of instruction and practice in advanced majors. On the employment front, we will meticulously design work experience and industry-academia connections—such as major-tailored employment support (responding to company-specific hiring procedures), expansion of the field practice semester system and Duksung internships, AI convergence job and startup expos, and the Dobong-Duksung Employment and Startup Festival—to produce tangible results." (“여대라고 하면 인문사회계열 위주의 대학이라고 오해한다. 하지만 우리 대학은 유아교육, 미술사학, 문화인류학 등 다양한 인문사회계열 전공 외에도 디지털소프트웨어공학 내 5개 트랙, 바이오공학, 식품영양학, 화학, 정보통계학 등 과학기술 관련 전공이 있다. 또한 미래인재대학에 AI신약학과, 데이터사이언스학과, 가상현실융합학과 등 ‘첨단’학과도 포진해 있다. 즉, 특정 학과에 ‘첨단’을 몰아주는 방식이 아니라 과학기술·데이터·콘텐츠·바이오 등 전공군 전체가 AI를 기본 역량으로 공유하는 구조가 갖춰져 있다는 것이 강점이다. 이를 뒷받침하기 위해 ‘AI 융합교육 지원센터’를 만들어 전공 수업에 바로 적용 가능한 AI-Wing 강의안·실습 템플릿·평가기준 제공, AI TA 매칭, 학생 AI 구독 지원 등을 추진해 첨단 전공의 수업·실습 품질을 끌어올리겠다. 취업 측면에서는 전공 맞춤형 취업지원(기업별 채용 절차 대응), 현장실습학기제·덕성인턴십 확대, AI 융합 취·창업박람회, 도봉-덕성 취창업 페스티벌 등 일경험·산학 연결을 촘촘히 설계해 성과를 만들어가겠다.”)

–Regarding educational innovation, your 'X+AI' initiative stands out. Can you explain it in detail? (–교육 혁신과 관련해 ‘X+AI’ 구상이 눈에 띄는데, 구체적으로 설명하면.)

"X+AI is not a matter of 'fitting majors around AI' but rather a structure where the major (X) is the core and AI serves as the wings. To this end, I have proposed: △Institutionalizing the 'Duksung Future Education Committee' under the direct authority of the president △Expanding the Center for Teaching and Learning Development into an 'AI Convergence Education Support Center' △Supporting AI teaching-student practice (TAs and student tutors) △Expanding flexible academic systems (P/NP, blended learning, code sharing, etc.). Additionally, on the research and industry-academia front, I will establish five 'X+AI Convergence Research Clusters' under the president's direct authority—digital humanities, AI drug discovery and bio-health, social data governance, AI art & tech, and AI-ESG climate and environment—so that education, research, and industry-academia are all interconnected." (“X+AI는 “AI 중심에 전공을 끼워 맞추는 방식”이 아니라, 전공(X)을 Core에 두고 AI를 Wing으로 활용하는 구조다. 이를 위해 △총장 직속 ‘덕성 미래교육 위원회’ 상설화 △교수학습개발센터의 ‘AI 융합교육 지원센터’ 확대 △AI 교수–학생 실습 지원(TA·학생 튜터) △유연 학사제도(P/NP, 블렌디드 러닝, 코드쉐어링 등) 확대를 제시했다. 또한, 연구·산학 측면에서는 총장 직속 ‘5대 X+AI 융합 연구 클러스터’(디지털 인문학, AI 신약·바이오헬스, 소셜데이터 거버넌스, AI 아트&테크, AI-ESG 기후환경) 구축을 통해 교육-연구-산학이 연결되도록 하겠다.”)

–You have said you will make 'Bright Duksung, Challenges Together' your operational principle during your term. Can you elaborate? (–임기 동안 ‘Bright 덕성, 함께하는 도전’을 대학의 운영 원칙으로 삼겠다고 했는데.)

"'Bright Duksung' is not just a slogan but an operational principle for the university. Based on six pillars—Balance, Respect, Innovation, Global, Harmony, and Talent—it is a vision to achieve harmony in education, research, and administration and realize a people-centered distinguished Duksung. The detailed operational principles are: △B (Balance): Balance between fiscal soundness and future investment △R (Respect): A campus where respect for students, faculty, and staff is institutionalized △I (Innovation): AI- and data-based innovation in education and administration △G (Global): Expanding international education infrastructure and making global experiences routine △H (Harmony): An educational philosophy where AI and HI (human intelligence) coexist △T (Talent): Tailored talent development with integrated support for career, employment, and entrepreneurship." (“‘Bright 덕성’은 단순한 슬로건이 아니라 대학 운영 원칙이다. 균형(Balance), 존중(Respect), 혁신(Innovation), 글로벌(Global), 조화(Harmony), 인재(Talent)라는 여섯 축을 바탕으로, 교육·연구·행정의 조화를 이루고, 사람 중심의 명문 덕성을 구현하겠다는 비전이다. 세부적인 운영 원칙은 △B(Balance): 재정 건전성과 미래 투자의 균형 △R(Respect): 학생·교수·직원의 존중이 제도로 구현되는 캠퍼스 △I(Innovation): AI·데이터 기반 교육·행정 혁신 △G(Global): 국제 교육 인프라 확충과 글로벌 경험의 일상화 △H(Harmony): AI와 HI(인간지능)가 공존하는 교육 철학 △T(Talent): 맞춤형 인재육성, 진로·취업·창업의 통합 지원으로 요약할 수 있겠다.”)

–Is there anything you would like to say in closing? (–끝으로 하고 싶은 말이 있다면.)

"In the AI era, universities cannot survive on rapid change alone. Ultimately, they must answer the question, 'What kind of people will we cultivate, and how?' That is why Duksung must become a place that respects the diversity of its majors while creating a 'human-centered advanced talent development model' where each major can grow on its own using AI as a tool. Throughout my four-year term, I will responsibly drive this process of change so that it earns the trust of our community, is felt by our students, and translates into tangible results for society." (“AI 시대에 대학은 빠른 변화만으로는 살아남기 어렵다. 결국은 ‘어떤 사람을 어떻게 길러낼 것인가’에 대한 답을 해야 한다. 그래서 덕성은 전공의 다양성을 존중하면서도, 각 전공이 AI를 도구로 삼아 스스로 성장할 수 있는 ‘사람 중심 첨단 인재양성 모델’을 만드는 곳이 되어야 한다. 4년간의 임기 동안 추진하고자 하는 그 변화의 과정이 구성원에게 신뢰받고, 학생에게 체감되며, 사회에 성과로 이어지도록 책임감 있게 추진하도록 하겠다.”)

Kim Mi-young, Reporter kimmy@hani.co.kr, Photo provided by Duksung Women's University (김미영 기자 kimmy@hani.co.kr, 사진 덕성여대 제공)

New Departments: Virtual Reality Convergence, Data Science, AI Drug Discovery (가상현실융합학과·데이터사이언스학과·AI신약학과 신설)

Full Free Major System Implemented... One Year of Academic and Career Exploration (전면 자유전공제 시행…1년간 학문과 진로 탐색)

( )

( )

Under the free major system, Duksung Women's University students do not declare a major upon admission. Instead, they enter under a broader division and spend their first year exploring diverse fields through major exploration courses and liberal arts courses, gaining extensive academic and career exploration time. They choose their major upon advancing to their second year, with the option to select their first major within their affiliated college and their second major from any college without restriction. This allows students to establish their identity and directly design their future according to their aptitudes and abilities. Starting with the 2025 academic year, a new Free Major Division has been established to provide even broader support for students' autonomous career design. (자유전공제에 따라 덕성여대 학생들은 입학 시 전공을 정하지 않고, 계열로 입학해 1년간 전공탐색과목과 교양과목을 통해 다양한 분야를 경험하며 폭넓은 학문과 진로 탐색의 시간을 갖는다. 2학년 진학 시 전공을 선택하게 되는데, 제1전공을 자신의 소속대학에서, 제2전공을 소속대학 구분 없이 선택할 수 있다. 이를 통해 학생들은 자신의 정체성을 바로 세우고, 자신의 적성과 능력에 따라 미래를 직접 설계할 수 있다. 2025학년도부터는 자유전공학부를 신설해 학생의 자율적 진로 설계를 더욱 폭 넓게 지원하고 있다.)

In addition, keeping pace with the AI era, the Future Talent College has successively established cutting-edge departments such as Virtual Reality Convergence, Data Science, AI Drug Discovery, and the Climate Environment and Culture major, building an academic structure that responds to future industrial demand. As a result, the university has earned an S grade—the highest rating—in the University Innovation Support Project performance evaluation for two consecutive years (2024 and 2025). The Korean Studies major and Korean Language Education program within the Future Talent College aim to become a cradle for cultivating K-content specialists. (여기에 더해 AI 시대에 발맞춰 미래인재대학에 가상현실융합학과, 데이터사이언스학과, AI신약학과, 기후환경과문화전공 등 첨단 분야 학과를 잇달아 신설하며 미래 산업 수요에 대응하는 학사구조를 갖춰가고 있다. 그 결과 2024년도 및 2025학년도 2년 연속 대학혁신지원사업 성과평가 최우수 등급인 S등급을 획득했다. 미래인재대학 내 한국학전공과 한국어교육과정은 K-콘텐츠 전문인력 양성의 요람으로 육성하는 것이 목표다.)

Since President Min Jae-hong took office, Duksung Women's University's innovation has shone even brighter. Plans are underway to gradually implement strengthening AI basic competency education, expanding interdisciplinary majors, revitalizing self-designed majors and Nano and Microdegree programs (intensive courses of 6–15 credits), and expanding code sharing (mutual recognition of specific courses through agreements between departments). (민재홍 총장 취임 후 덕성여대의 혁신은 한층 더 빛을 발하고 있다. AI 기초역량 교육 강화, 융합전공 확대, 자기설계전공과 나노(Nano)·마이크로디그리(Microdegree·6~15학점 규모의 심화 교육과정) 활성화, 코드셰어링(Code Sharing·학과 간 협약으로 특정 과목을 공동으로 인정) 확대 등을 점진적으로 추진할 계획이다.)

So that all students can develop AI utilization capabilities on the foundation of their majors, an 'AI Bridge' course will be developed, along with 'Duksung AI Literacy' classes and a support system for AI-integrated instruction in each major. Through these efforts, students will cultivate the ability to define and solve problems on their own, continuing the tradition of nurturing creative, convergent AI talent. Separately, the 'course retake system' is also slated to be converted into a 'grade forfeiture system.' (모든 학생이 전공 기반 위에서 AI 활용 역량을 갖출 수 있도록 ‘AI 브릿지’ 과목 개발 및 ‘덕성 AI 리터러시’ 수업, 전공별 AI 융합 수업 지원 체계도 구축되는데, 이를 통해 학생 스스로 문제를 정의하고 해결하는 힘까지 기르게 함으로써, 창의적 융·복합 AI 인재 양성의 전통을 이어가겠다는 것이다. 이와 별개로 ‘재수강 제도’의 ‘학점포기제’로 전환도 시행을 앞두고 있다.)

Kim Mi-young, Reporter (김미영 기자)

item.title: What Do Our Children's Gaming Habits Reveal About Their Personalities? (게임으로 알 수 있는 우리 아이들의 성향은?)
item.description:
Joo Hanna | Former Microsoft Researcher and Data Scientist
 
 At home, even if it doesn't quite rival the negotiation table of world leaders, a fierce "negotiation war" breaks out every single day—and it's about gaming time. ( 주한나 | 전 미국 마이크로소프트 연구원·데이터 과학자
 
 우리집에서는 세계 정상들의 국제관계 협상 테이블을 방불케하게까지는 않더라도 어쨌든 치열한 ‘네고전쟁’(negotiation war)이 매일같이 일어나는데 그것은 게임시간 관련이다.)

With smartphone and game addiction among youth emerging as a serious social issue, I'm surely not the only parent waging a battle over whether to allow gaming and for how long. (청소년의 스마트폰과 게임 중독의 문제가 심각한 사회 문제로 떠오른 만큼, 자녀의 게임 허용 여부와 시간을 놓고 전쟁을 벌이는 부모는 나뿐만이 아닐 것이다.)

Kids really love games. They likely spend far more time gaming than with school friends. No matter how much I lecture from the sidelines—saying that "games only inject an artificially manufactured sense of achievement, which is like junk food with no nutritional value, making it harder to find fulfillment in real life"—it has little effect. (아이들은 게임을 정말 좋아한다. 학교 친구와 보내는 시간보다 게임으로 보내는 시간이 훨씬 더 많을 것이다. 그 옆에서 내가 “게임은 인공적으로 만들어낸 가짜 성취감을 주입할 뿐이며, 이것은 곧 영양가 없는 정크 푸드와 같아서 실생활에서 성취감을 얻기 더 힘들게 한다”고 아무리 설교해봐야 별 효과는 없다.)

On the contrary, the child insists they experience achievement, challenge, cooperation, and world-building in games. If I can't understand what my child loves at all, it's hardly going to help improve our relationship. (오히려 아이는 게임에서 성취감, 도전, 협동, 세계 구축의 경험을 한다고 주장한다. 아이가 좋아하는 것을 내가 전혀 이해하지 못하면 관계 개선에 도움이 될 리가 없다.)

When a child makes a new friend, parents are extremely curious about what kind of kid they are. Games are no different. It's only natural for parents to wonder what games their children are playing. I've heard so much advice about needing to understand my children's games that I've tried it a few times myself. What I felt acutely is that there are far too many types to lump together under "games," and my children's tastes are so different from mine that I'd suspect a genetic anomaly. (아이가 새 친구를 사귀게 되면 부모는 그 아이가 어떤 아이인지 아주 궁금해한다. 게임도 마찬가지다. 부모가 자녀가 무슨 게임을 하는지 궁금해하는 것은 당연하다. 자녀가 하는 게임을 잘 알아야 한다는 조언을 하도 들어서 나도 몇 번 도전해보았다. 절절하게 느낀 것은 ‘게임’으로 뭉뚱그리기에는 너무나도 많은 종류가 있고, 아이들의 취향은 유전자가 의심될 정도로 나와 다르다는 것이다.)

So I asked artificial intelligence (AI) to broadly categorize game types. A child who enjoys FPS or battle royale games like Fortnite or Overwatch is drawn to immediate feedback and clear win-loss outcomes. They excel at momentary focus and enjoy making quick decisions under pressure. (그리하여 인공지능(AI)에게 게임 종류를 크게 나눠 달라고 부탁해보았다. 포트나이트, 오버워치 같은 FPS·배틀로얄을 즐기는 아이는 즉각적인 피드백과 명확한 승패에 끌린다. 순간 집중력이 뛰어나고 압박 상황에서 빠르게 판단하는 걸 좋아한다.)

A child who likes creative and sandbox games like Minecraft or The Sims enjoys the process more than the result. They thrive on building things up piece by piece and living off the pride of "I made this." (마인크래프트, 심즈 같은 창작·샌드박스 게임을 좋아하는 아이는 결과보다 과정을 즐긴다. 조금씩 쌓아가며 “내가 만들었다”는 자부심을 먹고 자란다.)

A child who enjoys social and party games like Among Us, Animal Crossing, or Mario Kart is relationship-oriented. Who they play with matters more than winning. They're suited for team sports or club activities, and careers like teaching, event planning, or HR roles fit their disposition well. (어몽어스, 동물의 숲, 마리오카트 같은 소셜·파티 게임을 즐기는 아이는 관계 중심적이다. 이기는 것보다 누구와 하는지가 더 중요하다. 팀 스포츠나 동아리 활동이 맞고, 교사·이벤트 기획자·HR 전문가가 적성과 잘 어울리는 직업이다.)

Of course, not every game fits neatly into these categories. Roblox alone is a platform containing millions of different experiences. Just saying "I play Roblox" doesn't tell you much about the child. What they do within it—sitting down beside them and looking into it together—is the most honest approach. A child opens up just from knowing that a parent cares about their world. (물론 모든 게임이 이런 식으로 각각 분류에 맞아 떨어지지 않는다. 로블록스만 해도 수백만 개의 서로 다른 체험이 담긴 플랫폼이다. “로블록스 한다”는 말만으로는 아이를 알 수 없다. 그 안에서 무엇을 하는지, 옆에 앉아서 함께 들여다보는 것이 가장 정직한 방법이다. 아이는 부모가 자기 세계에 관심을 가져준다는 것만으로도 마음을 연다.)

Once you have a general sense, using AI is a good option too. Input something like, "My child loves ○○ game; analyze this game's characteristics and recommend activities and aptitudes the child might enjoy," and you'll get a fairly detailed answer. Parents don't have to be gaming experts. They can also just ask the child directly. "What do you like most about the game?" Whether it's winning, building, the story, or playing with friends—that one answer reveals surprisingly much. (어느 정도 파악이 됐다면, AI를 활용하는 것도 좋다. “우리 아이가 ○○ 게임을 좋아하는데, 이 게임의 특성을 분석해서 아이가 좋아할 만한 활동과 적성을 추천해줘”라고 입력하면 꽤 구체적인 답이 돌아온다. 부모가 게임 전문가가 아니어도 된다. 아이에게 직접 물어봐도 된다. “게임에서 뭐가 제일 좋아?” 이기는 것인지, 만드는 것인지, 이야기인지, 친구랑 같이 하는 것인지. 그 대답 하나가 의외로 많은 걸 알려준다.)

Games don't have to be a waste of time. They can be a window into what draws a child in and how they experience the world. Before pulling the plug, let's first take a look inside the screen. (게임은 시간 낭비가 아닐 수 있다. 아이가 무엇에 끌리고, 어떤 방식으로 세계를 경험하는지를 보여주는 창일 수 있다. 전원을 뽑기 전에, 먼저 화면 속을 들여다보자.)

item.title: "It's okay without a stage, just add a spoonful of imagination" (“무대 없어도 괜찮아요, 상상력 한 스푼만 더하면”)
item.description:
The tvN entertainment program "After School Tae-ri Teacher" is making waves. It's a show where actress Kim Tae-ri opens an after-school theater class at a small rural elementary school and creates performances with children who have never done theater before. As they take on theater for the first time in their lives, the children gradually discover their own ways of expression. It doesn't matter if there's no stage or audience. Theater begins just by adding a spoonful of imagination to everyday life. This evening, pick up a picture book and say to your child, "Shall we act out this scene?" (tvN 예능 ‘방과후 태리쌤’이 화제다. 배우 김태리가 작은 시골 초등학교에 방과후 연극반을 열고, 연극이 처음인 아이들과 무대를 만들어가는 프로그램이다. 난생처음 연극에 도전하면서 아이들은 조금씩 자신만의 표현을 찾아간다. 꼭 무대와 관객이 갖춰지지 않아도 괜찮다. 일상에 상상력 한 스푼을 더하는 것만으로도 연극은 시작된다. 오늘 저녁, 그림책 한 권을 꺼내 아이에게 말해보자. “우리 이 장면 한번 연기해볼까?”)

Theater activities that safely open up the world of imagination (안전하게 상상의 세계를 열어주는 연극 활동)

When we think of theater, what comes to mind first is a dazzling stage, lighting, and actors performing passionately beneath it. That's why theater activities are appealing yet often seen as a field that's hard to take on easily. However, children actually experience theatrical activities naturally from a young age through play. Role-playing games in everyday life—like playing hospital, school, or grocery store—are exactly the starting point of theater. It's enough to have the mindset of expanding these role-playing games in a more systematic and diverse way. (연극이라고 하면 화려한 무대와 조명, 그 아래에서 열연을 펼치는 배우들의 모습이 먼저 떠오른다. 그래서 연극 활동은 매력적이지만 쉽게 도전하기 어려운 영역으로 여겨지기도 한다. 그러나 아이들은 사실 어릴 때부터 놀이를 통해 자연스럽게 연극적 활동을 경험한다. 병원놀이, 학교놀이, 마트놀이 등 일상에서 즐기는 역할 놀이가 바로 연극의 출발점이다. 이러한 역할 놀이를 좀더 체계적이고 다양하게 확장해본다는 마음이면 충분하다.)

Theater is a medium that lets children safely encounter various worlds on a fictional stage. They can freely experience situations in stories that would be hard to live through in reality, and by becoming characters different from themselves—animals, or even objects—they can develop empathy and a sense of self. It's also effective for building self-expression and proactiveness. (연극은 다양한 세상을 허구의 무대에서 안전하게 만나게 해주는 매개다. 아이들은 현실에서는 겪기 어려운 상황을 이야기 속에서 마음껏 경험하고, 나와 다른 인물이나 동물, 심지어 사물이 되어보는 과정을 통해 공감 능력과 자아를 키울 수 있다. 자기 표현력과 능동성을 키우는 데도 효과적이다.)

Lee Ji-hyun, a theater arts instructor and author of "Picture Book Theater Class" (School Library Journal Publishing), speaks to the benefits of theater activities: "A child with a quiet voice, a child who couldn't speak up in class, a child afraid of not having the right answer—through theater class activities, they find themselves raising their hand and speaking loudly without even realizing it." This applies not just to young children but to teenagers as well. During the period when self-identity is forming, the experience of acting out various characters helps them objectify themselves and understand others' perspectives. (‘그림책 연극 수업’((주)학교도서관저널)의 저자인 이지현 연극예술 강사는 “목소리가 작았던 아이, 발표를 못했던 아이, 정답이 아닐까 봐 무서워했던 아이가 연극 수업 활동을 하면서 자신도 모르게 손을 들고, 크게 말하게 된다”라면서 연극 활동의 효과를 이야기한다. 이는 유아·어린이뿐 아니라 청소년에게도 마찬가지다. 자아 정체성이 형성되는 시기에 다양한 인물을 연기해보는 경험은 자신을 객관화하고 타인의 관점을 이해하는 데 도움이 된다.)

Theatrical activities to try in everyday life (일상에서 시도해보는 연극적 활동)

–Seeing is believing: go watch a play first (–백문이 불여일견, 먼저 연극 보러 가기)

Before diving into theater activities, let's go see a live performance with your child. As you watch performances together, choosing ones that match your child's age and interests, the vivid energy of the stage and actors can naturally spark the feeling, "I want to try that too." Learning the etiquette of the theater—the rules to follow at a venue—is also a great experience. (연극 활동을 본격적으로 시작하기 전, 아이와 공연을 직접 보러 가보자. 아이의 연령대와 관심사에 맞는 공연을 골라 함께 관람하다 보면, 무대와 배우의 생생한 에너지를 통해 ‘나도 해보고 싶다’는 마음이 자연스럽게 생겨날 수 있다. 공연장에서 지켜야 할 약속, 즉 연극 에티켓을 함께 익히는 것도 좋은 경험이다.)

–Expressing with faces and bodies instead of words (–말 대신 표정과 몸짓으로 표현해보기)

If you're new to theater activities, start with a warm-up. Try a game where the caregiver and child look at cards with various emotion words and express them with facial expressions, then guess what each other is acting out. By silently acting out emotions like "a happy face," "a frightened face," or "an aggrieved face," children can learn about various feelings and ways to express them. (연극 활동이 처음이라면 워밍업부터 시작해보자. 보호자와 아이가 다양한 감정 단어 카드를 보면서 표정으로 표현하고 맞춰보는 게임을 추천한다. ‘기쁜 얼굴’ ‘겁에 질린 얼굴’ ‘억울한 얼굴’ 등 다양한 감정을 말없이 연기하면서 여러 감정과 표현 방법을 익혀나갈 수 있다.)

From there, you can also try pantomime, one of the theatrical methods of expression. It's a way of conveying a specific situation or emotion using only body movements, without any dialogue. You could pantomime a scene from a picture book or a play script, or act out a scene from daily life. (나아가 연극적 표현 방법 중 하나인 팬터마임을 시도해봐도 좋다. 대사 없이 몸짓만으로 특정 상황이나 감정을 표현하는 방식이다. 그림책이나 희곡 속 한 장면을 팬터마임으로 표현해볼 수도 있고, 일상 속 한 장면을 표현해봐도 된다.)

Instructor Lee Ji-hyun suggests, "How about trying to show—without speaking—everything from waking up this morning to stepping out the school front door, using only your face and body?" She notes that you can express routine actions through gestures. Along the way, you can point out parts that were left out or not expressed clearly, refining expressiveness together. (이지현 강사는 “오늘 아침에 일어나서 학교 현관을 나설 때까지 모습을 말하지 말고 표정과 행동으로만 표현해볼까?”라고 하면서 일상에서 자주 하는 행동을 몸짓으로 표현해볼 수 있다고 조언한다. 그 과정에서 생략되거나 표현이 부족한 부분들을 함께 짚으면서 표현력을 풍부하게 다듬을 수 있다.)

–Improvisational play using picture books (–그림책을 활용한 즉흥극 놀이)

Picture books are a great tool for theater activities. Lee Ji-hyun cites their accessibility as the biggest strength. "Picture books have little text and combine pictures with words, making them easy to approach. And the more you read them, the more you can discover something of your own in them." (그림책은 연극 활동에 활용할 수 있는 좋은 도구다. 이지현 강사는 그림책의 가장 큰 장점으로 만만함을 꼽는다. “그림책은 글밥이 적고 그림과 글이 함께 있어 접근이 쉬운 도구다. 동시에 읽을 수록 자신만의 무언가를 발굴해낼 수 있다는 매력도 있다.”)

Lee's "Picture Book Theater Class" introduces a variety of theater activities using picture books as a medium. You can choose books based on your child's age and interests and try out different theatrical expressions. For example, "I Shouldn't Have Taken It Off" is a picture book that playfully imagines a child who gets stuck while taking off clothes and flails around. After reading it, you can imagine a similar situation and act it out as an improvisational play. (이지현 강사의 ‘그림책 연극 수업’에는 그림책을 매개로 한 다양한 연극 활동이 소개되어 있다. 아이의 연령과 관심사에 따라 그림책을 선택하고 여러 연극적 표현을 시도해볼 수 있다. 일례로 ‘벗지 말걸 그랬어’는 옷을 벗다가 걸려서 버둥거리는 아이의 이야기를 재미있는 상상력으로 담아낸 그림책이다. 이 책을 읽고 그림책과 같은 상황을 상상하고 즉흥극으로 표현해볼 수 있다.)

When doing theater activities with picture books, start by simply following the scenes or dialogue as written. Once comfortable, you can expand endlessly—by changing the ending or introducing new characters. (그림책으로 연극 활동을 할 때 처음에는 책의 장면이나 대사를 그대로 따라하는 것으로 시작, 익숙해지면 결말을 바꾸거나 새로운 캐릭터를 등장시키는 방식으로 얼마든지 확장할 수 있다.)

–Today I'm the mom: role-swapping activities (–오늘은 내가 엄마, 역할 바꾸기 활동)

Try swapping roles and acting them out. A caregiver and child can trade places, or close friends can act as each other. When a caregiver and child do role-play in particular, the child gets an indirect experience of the parent's position, and the parent can gain a chance to think from the child's point of view. At this point, if you deliberately act out only the things your child usually does wrong in an attempt to teach a lesson, it could actually increase resentment toward the activity. Instead, by observing the other person closely and capturing their traits, let it become a moment to reaffirm affection for each other. With a teenage child, this can even open up subtle conflicts that were hard to address in everyday conversation and break the ice for communication. (서로의 역할을 바꾸어 연기해보자. 보호자와 아이가 역할을 바꿀 수도 있고, 친한 친구끼리 서로를 연기해볼 수도 있다. 특히 보호자와 아이가 역할극을 하면 아이는 부모의 입장을 간접적으로 경험하고, 부모 역시 아이의 입장에서 생각해보는 계기를 만들 수 있다. 이때 아이에게 교훈을 주려는 목적으로 평소 아이가 잘 못하는 부분만 연기하면 활동에 대한 반감이 오히려 커질 수 있다. 상대방을 잘 관찰하고 특징을 표현함으로써, 오히려 서로에 대한 애정을 확인하는 계기로 삼아보자. 청소년 자녀와 함께하면 평소 대화로는 하기 어려웠던 미묘한 갈등을 드러내고 소통의 물꼬를 트는 뜻밖의 효과를 볼 수도 있다.)

Want to go further? Put on a performance (조금 더 나아가고 싶다면, 공연 올리기)

If you want to take it a step further, you can even try putting on a live stage performance. Rehearsing and staging a complete play gives children an unforgettable experience. It doesn't have to be grand. Start by putting on a short show just for the family. You could gather neighborhood kids to prepare a play together, or set up a class theater stage in the classroom. (한 단계 더 나아가 직접 무대 공연까지 시도해봐도 좋다. 한편의 완결된 연극을 연습하고 무대에 올리는 일은 아이들에게 잊을 수 없는 경험을 선사한다. 거창하지 않아도 괜찮다. 가족끼리 짧은 공연을 올리는 것부터 시작해보자. 동네 아이들을 모아 함께 연극을 준비하거나, 교실에서 학급 연극 무대를 꾸며봐도 좋다.)

When preparing a performance, first choose a script or story. You can use a picture book, or find a suitable script online. Teenagers could even adapt an original novel or film themselves. Once the script is set, take time to explore the plot, character traits, and emotions together. After assigning roles, read the script aloud in character, and decide together where to stand and how to move—the stage blocking. For costumes and props, what you have at home is more than enough. Mom's scarf becomes a king's cape, and an umbrella transforms into a magic wand. The very process of imagining what each object could become and building the stage is a wonderful creative activity in itself. The moment the performance ends and everyone applauds each other, the child feels the achievement of having created something together with their whole body. (공연을 준비할 때는 대본이나 이야기를 먼저 고른다. 그림책을 활용해도 좋고, 인터넷에서 적절한 대본을 찾는 방법도 있다. 청소년이라면 원작 소설이나 영화를 직접 각색해볼 수도 있다. 대본이 정해지면 줄거리와 인물의 성격, 감정을 함께 탐색하는 시간을 갖자. 배역이 정해지면 각자 맡은 인물로 대본을 소리 내어 읽어보고, 어느 위치에서 어떻게 움직일지 동선을 함께 정한다. 의상이나 소품은 집에 있는 것들을 활용하면 충분하다. 엄마의 스카프가 왕의 망토가 되고, 우산이 마법 지팡이로 변신한다. 어떤 물건이 무엇으로 변할 수 있을지 상상하며 무대를 꾸미는 과정 자체가 훌륭한 창작 활동이다. 공연이 끝난 후 서로에게 박수를 보내는 그 순간, 아이는 함께 무언가를 만들어냈다는 성취감을 온몸으로 느끼게 된다.)

Systematic theater activities through programs (프로그램으로 만나는 체계적인 연극 활동)

It's also worth looking into programs led by professional instructors. They offer a more systematic and professional way to experience and learn theater. Local cultural foundations, libraries, children's theater troupes, and similar organizations offer a wide range of programs for children. (전문 강사가 이끄는 프로그램을 찾아보는 것도 추천한다. 더 체계적이고 전문적인 방법으로 연극을 접하고 배울 수 있다. 각 지역의 문화재단, 도서관, 어린이 극단 등에서 아이들을 대상으로 한 관련 프로그램을 다양하게 찾아볼 수 있다.)

SeoSuwon Library will hold an experiential 3D narration performance called "Book Play Theater" on April 12. In this program, participants meet the stories "The Farting Daughter-in-Law" and "Red Bean Porridge Grandma and the Tiger" alongside a polar bear character, and can follow along with songs and movements. It's aimed at children aged 5 through 2nd grade of elementary school. Registration is available through the SeoSuwon Library website and the Suwon City Library app. (서수원도서관은 오는 4월12일 체험형 입체낭독극 ‘책놀이 연극’을 진행한다. 북극곰 캐릭터와 함께 ‘방귀쟁이 며느리’ ‘팥죽할머니와 호랑이’ 이야기를 만나며 노래와 율동을 직접 따라 해볼 수 있는 프로그램으로, 만 5살부터 초등학교 2학년을 대상으로 한다. 참가 신청은 서수원도서관 누리집과 수원시도서관 앱에서 할 수 있다.)

In Gwangju, the Asia Culture Center Foundation is recruiting members for the "Dream Theater Gwangju Dong-gu" for local children and youth. The program runs every Thursday from April 23 to November 22, and is a creative activity where participants experience the entire process of making a performance firsthand. Tuition is fully free, and details can be found on the foundation's website (www.accf.or.kr). (광주에서는 국립아시아문화전당재단이 지역 아동·청소년을 위한 ‘꿈의 극단 광주 동구’ 단원을 모집한다. 오는 4월23일부터 11월22일까지 매주 목요일 진행하는 해당 프로그램은 공연이 만들어지는 전 과정을 직접 체험하는 창작 활동이다. 교육비는 전액 무료이며, 자세한 내용은 재단 누리집(www.accf.or.kr)에서 확인하면 된다.)

Dream Theater Gwanak is a culture and arts education program for teenagers. In 2026, it is recruiting a second cohort of members for "We Are Heroes," a program where participants complete a full musical performance through expression training in acting, vocalization, and choreography, as well as creative processes. The activity runs from April to November, with applications accepted until April 7. Details and inquiries are available through the Gwanak Cultural Foundation (gfac.or.kr). (꿈의 극단 관악은 청소년을 대상으로 하는 문화예술교육 프로그램이다. 2026년에는 연기, 발성, 안무 등의 표현 교육과 창작 과정을 통해 하나의 뮤지컬 공연을 완성하는 ‘우리가 영웅’ 2기 단원을 모집한다. 활동기간은 4월부터 11월까지이며, 4월 7일까지 참여자를 모집한다. 자세한 사항 확인 및 문의는 관악문화재단(gfac.or.kr)에서 가능하다.)

Park Eun-ah, contributing reporter (박은아 객원기자)

]]>

item.title: “Mom Will Listen—Go Ahead and Talk” (“엄마가 들어 줄게, 말이나 해보렴”)
item.description:
Park Mi-ja | Author of ‘Middle School Years, the Age That Works Miracles’ and Research Professor at Sungkonghoe University

Your child slams the front door in frustration over something that happened outside and storms into their room. If you knock and go in, they’re fuming and blaming everyone else. What’s the best way to handle this? ( 박미자 | ‘중학생, 기적을 부르는 나이’ 저자·성공회대 연구교수

 아이가 밖에서 있었던 일로 짜증을 내며 현관문을 쾅 닫고 자기 방으로 들어갑니다. 노크를 하고 들어가면, 화를 내며 씩씩거리고 남 탓이나 합니다. 이럴 경우에는 어떻게 하는 것이 좋을까요?)

From a parent’s perspective, it’s truly exasperating. But it’s important to remember that the one who’s actually struggling is the child. From the child’s point of view, the irritation and venting are a message expressing how hard things are for them. They’re clumsily reaching out for comfort from anyone. In this situation, rather than scolding with “Why are you so grumpy when you come home?” or “You should just be more patient,” it’s better to convey a message of attentive listening—showing you understand their side and are willing to hear them out. <<> “Welcome home.” <<> “Ugh, I’m so pissed.” <<> “What happened?” <<> “You wouldn’t get it, Mom. You can’t help anyway…” <<> “Sounds like you had a rough time. I’m grateful you held it together and made it home.” <<> “......” <<> “When you’re feeling stuck, it can help to at least talk it out. Mom will listen—go ahead and talk…” <<> The child starts venting about what happened with their friends, rambling in a jumbled way (if they went straight to their room, knocking a little later to invite a conversation or offering a drink to break the ice works well too). It’s essential to listen while empathizing with the child’s feelings. Once the child’s anger subsides through conversation and their heart settles, they may begin to find understanding for the friend who upset them. <<> “Don’t you think that friend might have had some reason they couldn’t help?” <<> At first, the child snapped at their mom and talked back, but as the mom calmly kept the conversation going and listened, the child was able to reflect on their relationship with the friend and develop a sense of understanding toward them. <<> The most precious gift caregivers can give to adolescents in their daily lives isn’t lecturing or offering solutions—it’s the time spent truly listening to what the child has to say. <<> When a teenager complains about a teacher, it’s better for parents to listen rather than jump in to judge right from wrong or try to fix the problem. Saying things like “Oh, that’s too bad,” “Why do you think that happened?” “What could you do?” “That must have been hard,” and “Thanks for telling me” gives the child a chance to reflect on the situation on their own. <<> Teenagers act out because they feel anxious and insecure. They want their parents to be on their side and to feel trusted by them, but they’re still at a stage of growing through unsteadiness. If they sense that their parents don’t believe in them or are defending someone else, anxiety about themselves and resentment toward their parents build up inside, leaving them unstable. <<> We’ve all had moments in daily life where someone simply listened to us, and while talking through a tough situation, we came up with our own solution. In a way, conversation isn’t a process for solving problems—it’s a process of giving each other time to think. <<> Adolescence is a time when young people meet all kinds of people, clash and accept, broaden their social relationships, and learn how to live as the masters of their own lives. It’s a period when they love their parents deeply but grow with the task of living independently in their own way, rather than following in their parents’ footsteps. (부모님 입장에서는 정말 답답하지요. 그런데, 정작 힘든 사람은 아이라는 사실을 기억해야 합니다. 아이 입장에서 보면, 짜증과 화풀이도 자신의 힘든 상황을 표현하는 메시지라고 할 수 있습니다. 누구에게라도 위로받고 싶은 마음을 서툰 방식으로 표현하는 것입니다. 이런 상황에서는 부모가 “왜 집에 와서 짜증이냐?” “네가 좀 참으면 되잖아” 같은 훈계보다는 네 입장을 이해하고 들어주겠다는 경청의 메시지를 표현하는 방식을 권합니다.)
